title: Dominic and the Archive Revisited
premise: Odile Fairweather, the last xenolinguist on the dying colony of Meridian's Rest, has spent years recording its slow abandonment while losing their ability to dream in any human tongue. When a name that shouldn't exist appears on the manifest of a ship that never launched, Odile discovers they are the unwitting carrier of an encoded message from the colony's founders — one capable of ending, or igniting, the war between Earth and the alien Archive. Hunted by both sides and betrayed by the friend who kept them invisible, Odile must decode and deliver the message before the colony's final evacuation window closes. In the end, Odile broadcasts it openly to both fleets, sacrificing their own escape and accepting inheritance of the Archive's voice — ending the war at the cost of never going home.
about_author: Juniper Halloran is a former field linguist turned novelist who writes about the places history decides to forget. They live in a coastal town where the fog arrives earlier every year, and they insist this is relevant.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Odile records the emptying market district of Meridian's Rest, noting in their journal that they dreamed last night in a language with no human words. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: quiet grief and denial — the colony is dying, and so is something inside them.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Auditing the colonial archive for a routine report, Odile finds the freighter Vespera listed as launched with full crew — yet it still sits in the scrapyard, and the manifest bears a name Odile has never heard but somehow can pronounce. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile tracks the impossible name to a sealed founder-era vault beneath the old comms tower. Inside: recordings in the Archive's language, addressed by name to whoever found them. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the thrill of being chosen.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Kept Me Small
chapters.summary: Odile confides in Sefa, the colony administrator who has quietly protected them for years — and realizes Sefa already knew about the vault. Sefa admits she engineered Odile's obscurity to keep the message dormant. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing a whole life.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Are Listening
chapters.summary: An Earth survey drone and an Archive probe arrive within hours of each other; both sides now know the message exists. Sefa urges destruction; Odile begins translating instead. POV: alternating Odile and intercepted transmissions. Emotional beat: hunted, cornered, defiant.

chapters.title: Dreaming in the Enemy Tongue
chapters.summary: Deep translation work dissolves what remains of Odile's human-language dreams; the message turns out to be the Archive's terms for coexistence, written in the founders' blood-oath cipher. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: transformation — the loss becomes fluency.

chapters.title: Evacuation Window
chapters.summary: Earth forces move to seize the colony ahead of schedule; Sefa offers Odile a place on the last shuttle if they hand over the decoded message for military use. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit — safety in exchange for complicity.

chapters.title: What the Founders Owed
chapters.summary: Odile uncovers the final layer: the founders stole the Archive's voice to build the colony, and the message is restitution. The war began as an unpaid debt of inheritance. POV: Odile, with founder recordings interleaved. Emotional beat: horrified clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: As both fleets converge, Odile seizes the comms tower and transmits the message unencrypted to everyone — Earth, the Archive, the fleeing colonists — then stays at the console as the shuttle leaves without them. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: climax; terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive Revisited
chapters.summary: Ceasefire settles over Meridian's Rest like snow. The Archive answers Odile directly, offering not rescue but continuation: a shared voice, a rebuilt colony, a debt honored. Odile dreams, finally, in two languages at once. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — home redefined rather than regained.
